_about: The closing section of the suite results document, the interpretation layer the owner's review asked for. `intro`: the paragraphs of C.1 before the observations. `observations`: a list of {id, template}; each template is one sentence the generator fills from the run with the placeholders listed under `placeholders` (sections.closing_values); an observation whose values the run lacks prints as 'not computed'; an interpretive clause is a conditional `[[flag ? when true | when false]]` on a flag computed from the run (a bool, false without data; facts.fill), so that it prints only when the run's figures make it true (VERIFY-R4, issue 2). No sentence states a timing cause: what the run measures is stated, and what it does not isolate (the host's load, the service's queue, the cache, the loop's order, the answers' sizes) is named as not isolated (the owner's second review, point 3; VERIFY-R4, issue 1). `caveats`: the paragraphs after the observations (the shared host load; cold / warm as the recorded heuristic); the load clauses of the caveats and of C3's limits ('observed under concurrent host load', 'carried the Logan load') are conditional on `logan_caveat`, the flag of the sampler's means (the v5 merge, 2026-10-15). `plots`: the captions keyed paired_latency and phases (C.2). `sections`: per table section (C3 MCP overhead decomposition, C4 front cost, C5 cold versus warm, C6 load telemetry, C7 per-chapter timing) a method paragraph, an observation paragraph with the run's figures and sample sizes as placeholders, and a limits paragraph, printed above the tables. The tables keep compare.json's figures. No stacked bar of phase medians: their sum is not the median of the wall. Inline markup: `code` and *emphasis*. Placeholders of overview.json (database, k, ...) work here too.

_assumes._note: The literal numbers this file's prose may carry, each with its source: constants of the SPEC, of the manifest v4 (lengths, budgets, expected runs), of the service's table or of the harness, never a figure of a run (those are placeholders the generator fills). tests/test_doc.py fails on a number the prose carries that is listed neither here nor as a placeholder; add a constant here with its source, never a run's figure.
_assumes.1: the pairs within 1 s (sections.closing_values); repeat 1 (the harness)
_assumes.100: a container peak above 100 % CPU (docker stats)

placeholders.mcp_over_local_p50 / _p90 / _max / _n: compare.json summary.mcp_overhead.minus_local_ms (warm MCP wall minus direct-local's first warm wall), signed
placeholders.backend_over_local_p50 / _p90 / _n: summary.mcp_overhead.backend_minus_local_ms (the service-timed host call minus direct-local), signed
placeholders.phase_submit_p50 / _p90 / _max / _n: summary.mcp_phases.submit_ms: per paired scenario the warm MCP execution's phase (repeat 1 preferred), zeros included; likewise phase_queue_*, phase_backend_*, phase_terminal_lag_*, phase_paging_*, phase_backend_pattern_*
placeholders.front_net_p50 / _p90 / _n: the per-scenario front_overhead.net_ms of compare.json (direct-remote minus direct-local, net of the server time), pooled over every scenario
placeholders.warm_wall_dl_p50 / _p90 / _n: the first host-warm wall per scenario on direct-local (warm after an interrupted execution excluded); likewise warm_wall_dr_*, warm_wall_mcp_*
placeholders.paired_dl_mcp_n / _ratio_p50 / _ratio_p1: the scenarios with a host-warm wall on both direct-local and mcp: their count, the ratio mcp / direct-local (p50, p10, p90), the difference (signed) and how many pairs lie within 1 s of each other in either direction (|difference| below 1 s)
placeholders.paired_dl_dr_n / _delta_p50 / _delta_p90: the scenarios with a host-warm wall on both direct arms: their count and the difference direct-remote minus direct-local
placeholders.load_samples / load_sra_mean / load_sra_: the sampler's figures (report.load_figures) and whether the Logan caveat applies ('applies' / 'does not apply')
placeholders.warm_after_interrupted_n: executions that ran warm after an interrupted one (counted in no bucket)
placeholders.mcp_phase_largest / mcp_phase_largest_p5: the phase of summary.mcp_phases (submit, queue, backend, terminal lag, paging) with the largest p50, in words, and that p50
placeholders.load_caveat_line: one sentence: the Logan caveat applies (the sra_all CPU mean and the load1 mean over the samples) or does not
placeholders.paired_dl_mcp_faster: the pairs where the warm MCP wall was below direct-local's
placeholders.scenarios_without_mcp_local_pair / _remo: the scenarios the MCP overhead pairing leaves out: every scenario less the pairs against direct-local (remote)
placeholders.cold_mcp_all_p50 / _p90 / _max / _n: summary.front_overhead.cold[mcp].wall_ms: every host-cold MCP execution (C.4's host-cold table), a larger population than mcp_cold_wall_* (the cold calls of the scenarios with a backend-timed MCP pair)
placeholders.phase_paging_zero_n / phase_paging_nonze: of the phases' population, the executions whose paging took 0 ms (the results came with the terminal status) and the others; the log-scale box plot draws the others only
placeholders.cold_mcp_untimed_n: the host-cold MCP executions C.4 counts that C.3's cold-wall population leaves out: cold_mcp_all_n minus mcp_cold_wall_n (the calls without a backend timing)
placeholders.paired_dl_wall_p50 / paired_mcp_wall_p50: the medians of the two sides of the paired population (the direct-local walls, the warm MCP walls of the same scenarios)
placeholders.paired_seconds_to_milliseconds: flag: the paired medians print in seconds (mcp) and in milliseconds (direct-local), as cells.fmt_t prints them
placeholders.mcp_over_local_positive / backend_share_: flags: the median MCP overhead against direct-local is positive; the median backend overhead against direct-local is below half of it (sections.BACKEND_SHARE_SMALL)
placeholders.cold_warm_mcp_close: flag: the MCP cold-warm median ratio is within a quarter of one (sections.COLD_WARM_CLOSE)
placeholders.cold_mcp_untimed_text: the same calls split by what ended them, computed from the record (sections.cold_mcp_untimed_split: the outcome and the recorded time limitation, e.g. 'the host's /pattern 503 deadline relayed by the service', else the error code in words), largest group first: '23 by design (...), 3 inconclusive (the host's /resolve 503 deadline relayed by the service) and 1 inconclusive (the service's own deadline, `resolve_timeout`)'

title: Cross-cutting timing
intro: What this section measures: the timings of this run as recorded, keyed on the host-cache heuristic of I.2 and read across the chapters; the observations below are computed from the run with their sample sizes, and the sections after the plots give each table its method, its observation and its limits. What it does not measure: the host's cache (a recency heuristic, never residency), the service's floor (one deployment, one day, under the host's load) or an end-to-end total (the phases' medians are never summed).

observations.template: Via MCP a host-warm request took {mcp_over_local_p50} longer than on direct-local at the median and {mcp_over_local_p90} at p90 (n {mcp_over_local_n} pairs; {mcp_over_local_no_queue_p50} and {mcp_over_local_no_queue_p90} with the queue wait taken out).

The host call as the service timed it differs from direct-local's wall by {backend_over_local_p50} at the median (p90 {backend_over_local_p90}, n {backend_over_local_n})[[mcp_over_local_positive ?[[backend_share_small ?: at the median the host call carries less than half of the MCP overhead; the rest lies in the service's own phases (C.3) |: at the median the host call carries half or more of the MCP overhead]]]].

Of the phases (per scenario its host-warm MCP execution with a backend timing, n {phase_backend_n}), {mcp_phase_largest} has the largest median ({mcp_phase_largest_p50}); at the median submit takes {phase_submit_p50}, the queue {phase_queue_p50}, the backend {phase_backend_p50} and paging {phase_paging_p50}; the phases are shown side by side and never summed, since their medians do not add up to the wall's.

Per scenario the warm MCP wall is {paired_dl_mcp_ratio_p50} times direct-local's at the median (p10 {paired_dl_mcp_ratio_p10}, p90 {paired_dl_mcp_ratio_p90}; n {paired_dl_mcp_n}; the two medians {paired_mcp_wall_p50} against {paired_dl_wall_p50}[[paired_seconds_to_milliseconds ?, seconds against milliseconds]]); in {paired_dl_mcp_under_1s} of the {paired_dl_mcp_n} pairs the two walls lie within 1 s of each other, and in {paired_dl_mcp_faster} the MCP call was the faster one.

The public front costs {front_net_p50} per request at the median net of the server time (p90 {front_net_p90}, n {front_net_n}), plus a connection set-up of {connect_dr_p50} (p90 {connect_dr_p90}) against {connect_dl_p50} on the container's port.

Warm minus cold per scenario is {cold_warm_mcp_delta_p50} at the median via MCP (ratio {cold_warm_mcp_ratio_p50}, n {cold_warm_mcp_n}) and {cold_warm_dl_delta_p50} on direct-local (n {cold_warm_dl_n})[[cold_warm_mcp_close ?: via MCP the median warm execution is within a quarter of its cold one, so the host-cache heuristic separates the two little in this run |: via MCP the median warm execution is more than a quarter off its cold one in this run]].

The host's `sra_all` CPU averaged {load_sra_mean} % and load1 {load_load1_mean} over {load_samples} samples, so the Logan caveat {load_caveat}; {warm_after_interrupted_n} executions ran warm after an interrupted one and are in no bucket.

caveats: {load_caveat_line} Every timing in this section is the shared host's[[logan_caveat ?, observed under concurrent host load]]: not a baseline for the release.

Cold and warm are the recorded heuristic (a scenario's first execution to reach the host, then any within {warm_window_s} s of another ending on the host), not a measurement of residency; a delta between them is the difference of two executions in the loop's order, and the loop's order is the only control.

plots.paired_latency: Paired host-warm walls per scenario: the warm MCP call against direct-local (left, n {paired_dl_mcp_n}) and direct-remote against direct-local (right, n {paired_dl_dr_n}); log scales, the dashed line y = x. One point per scenario; nothing is summed.
plots.phases: The MCP phases, per scenario of its host-warm MCP execution with a backend timing (the population of C.3's table, n {phase_backend_n}), one box per phase: the box p25 to p75, the line p50, the whiskers p10 and p90, log scale; the second line of a tick label is the box's n. Paging is 0 ms where the results came with the terminal status ({phase_paging_zero_n} of {phase_paging_n}); a log scale cannot hold them, so the paging box draws the {phase_paging_nonzero_n} others and sits above the table's median. The phases are drawn side by side, not summed: their medians do not add up to an end-to-end total.

C3.title: MCP overhead decomposition
paragraphs: *Method.* Pairs of host-warm executions only: the MCP warm execution (repeat 1 preferred) minus each direct arm's first host-warm execution of the same scenario, {mcp_over_local_n} pairs against direct-local and {mcp_over_remote_n} against direct-remote. The phases are the service's own measurements of one MCP execution per scenario, its host-warm execution with a backend timing (repeat 1 preferred; n {phase_backend_n}, zeros included; the box plot of C.2 draws the same population, its paging box without the {phase_paging_zero_n} zeros): submit (the tool's acknowledgement), queue (the job created to started), backend (the host call), terminal lag (the job finished to the client seeing it) and paging (fetching the results).

*Observation.* The MCP arm's wall time exceeds direct-local's by {mcp_over_local_p50} at the median and {mcp_over_local_p90} at the 90th percentile ({mcp_over_local_no_queue_p50} and {mcp_over_local_no_queue_p90} with the queue wait taken out), and direct-remote's by {mcp_over_remote_p50} at the median; the host call itself, as the service timed it, is {backend_over_local_p50} longer than the direct-local wall at the median and {backend_over_local_p90} at p90, the public URL and the front being in it. The phase with the largest median is {mcp_phase_largest} ({mcp_phase_largest_p50}). The phases' medians are medians of separate distributions: they are not summed, because their sum is not the median of the wall. A cold MCP call (the scenario's first on the host) took {mcp_cold_wall_p50} at the median and {mcp_cold_wall_p90} at p90 (n {mcp_cold_wall_n}: the backend-timed cold calls); every host-cold MCP execution, the {cold_mcp_untimed_n} without a backend timing among them ({cold_mcp_untimed_text}), is in C.4's host-cold table (n {cold_mcp_all_n}, p90 {cold_mcp_all_p90}).

*Limits.* The pairs leave out cold MCP executions, executions warm after an interrupted one and the {scenarios_without_mcp_local_pair} scenarios without a host-warm pair against direct-local ({scenarios_without_mcp_remote_pair} against direct-remote): those the tools could not express, those the service decided at submit and those without a host-warm execution on one side. [[logan_caveat ? The service ran on its own host and the MetaGraph host carried the Logan load (C.6), so the overhead is this run's, not the service's floor. | The service ran on its own host and the MetaGraph host under the load C.6 records, so the overhead is this run's, not the service's floor.]] The backend rows are the host call as the service timed it (the public URL and the front in it) against each direct arm; the wall rows hold that call and the service's own phases; the run does not isolate the host's load from the service's queue in either.

C4.title: Front cost
paragraphs: *Method.* direct-remote minus direct-local on host-warm pairs of the same scenario, net of the server time (the host's own elapsed time cancels, so the difference is the network, the front and the client), per chapter; a fresh connection's set-up (TCP, and TLS on the public URL) is recorded apart as the connect time.

*Observation.* The front and the network add {front_net_p50} at the median and {front_net_p90} at p90 over {front_net_n} pairs; a fresh connection costs {connect_dr_p50} at the median and {connect_dr_p90} at p90 on the public URL (n {connect_dr_n}) against {connect_dl_p50} on localhost. The host-cold table at the end counts every host-cold execution per arm; on mcp that is the arm's whole cold column (n {cold_mcp_all_n}), the {cold_mcp_untimed_n} calls without a backend timing included ({cold_mcp_untimed_text}), which is why its n and p90 exceed C.3's cold-wall figures.

*Limits.* {scenarios_without_warm_pair} scenarios have no host-warm pair of the two direct arms (the long scenarios not run on direct-remote among them) and {warm_pairs_left_out_after_interrupted} pairs warm after an interrupted execution are left out. The server time is netted out, so a chapter's net cost holds the network, the front and the client; the run records each answer's body size but does not isolate its effect, so a chapter's net cost above the run's median is assigned neither to its answers' sizes nor to anything else; the laptop's own load is in the remote wall and is not sampled.

C5.title: Cold versus warm
paragraphs: *Method.* Per scenario the warm execution minus the cold one on the same arm (the delta, signed: negative when warm was faster) and warm over cold (the ratio). Only an arm with both states has pairs: mcp, cold then warm by construction ({cold_warm_mcp_n} pairs), and direct-local where a direct execution was the first on the host ({cold_warm_dl_n} pairs). Cold and warm are the recorded recency heuristic of I.2 (the scenario's first execution to reach the host; another within {warm_window_s} s), not a measured cache state.

*Observation.* On mcp the median delta is {cold_warm_mcp_delta_p50} and the p90 {cold_warm_mcp_delta_p90}, the median ratio {cold_warm_mcp_ratio_p50}; on direct-local the median delta is {cold_warm_dl_delta_p50}, the p90 {cold_warm_dl_delta_p90} and the median ratio {cold_warm_dl_ratio_p50} over {cold_warm_dl_n} pairs (a figure over fewer than about thirty pairs is anecdotal).

*Limits.* A negative median with a positive p90 says that most warm repeats were somewhat faster and some much slower; the record does not isolate the service's queue, the host's load of that minute and the cache from one another, so the slower ones are assigned to none of them. The heuristic cannot see what the host had cached before the run or whether another client warmed a row between the two calls, and the paired loop's order (direct after the cold MCP call) is the only control.

C6.title: Load telemetry
paragraphs: *Method.* docker stats of the staging container (CPU, memory) and of the `sra_all` container (the Logan indexing load) and the host load average, sampled every 2 s on mex and joined to each execution's window; per chapter and arm the table gives the container's peak CPU and memory, the `sra_all` CPU mean and the load1 mean over the executions.

*Observation.* {load_samples} samples; `sra_all` CPU mean {load_sra_mean} % (max {load_sra_max} %), load1 mean {load_load1_mean} (max {load_load1_max}), so the Logan caveat {load_caveat} (the thresholds: {load_caveat_sra_cpu_pct} % `sra_all` CPU or a load1 of {load_caveat_load1}, half of mex's cores).

*Limits.* The figures are the shared host's context, not the request's own cost: a container peak above 100 % says a chapter's requests ran threads in parallel, the memory peak is the loaded index's residency, and the `sra_all` and load1 columns say how busy the host was while each chapter ran. Nothing here attributes a slow execution to the load; it says only under which load it ran.

C7.title: Per-chapter timing
paragraphs: *Method.* Wall and server time per chapter, arm and host-cache state, as p50, p90 and max with n; {warm_after_interrupted_n} execution(s) warm after an interrupted execution are in neither bucket.

*Reading.* Compare arms within one chapter and one host state only. The server time is the host's own elapsed time on the request and contains neither the front nor the service, so a direct-remote server time that differs from direct-local's on the same chapter is a difference between two executions in the loop's order (direct-remote runs third); the run does not isolate the loop's order from the host's load. A gap between a chapter's host-cold p90 and its host-warm p90 is measured on the recorded heuristic; what the host had cached, the loop's order and the load are not isolated from one another, and the cold figures are those of each scenario's first execution on the host in this run.

*Limits.* The cold buckets of the direct arms are small by construction (a direct execution is cold only when the MCP call before it never reached the host), so their percentiles are those of a few scenarios; the mcp cold bucket is the whole arm. The Logan caveat of C.1 {load_caveat} to every figure here.
